text: When exact numbers matter more than shape, you reach for one of two visuals. Here's the more powerful one.

A matrix works like an Excel PivotTable — fields on rows and columns both, automatically aggregated at every intersection. Year and Quarter down the side, Subcategory and Product across the top, Units Sold filling every cell.
Plus and minus icons on the headers let viewers drill into more detail or collapse back to a summary — or turn on Auto expand to show every level the moment the visual loads.
And by default, row headers stay frozen as the matrix scrolls horizontally — category labels never disappear off screen, no matter how many columns you're comparing.
